metas.name: Arid Landscape
metas.note: In the center and more towards the south, the climate becomes warmer and drier. The landscape is more arid. Forests are considerably more rare, and make way for shrubs and open fields. The difference is not extreme, but can become noticeable after some practice.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Baltic Pines
metas.note:
Forests with Baltic pines (Pinus sylvestris) are most commonly found in the north, most often near the border with Belarus. Baltic pines are usually tall and have orange-red bark.

NOTE: Note that the Carpathians are also covered in a lot of pine forests. They are noticeably hilly however, allowing you to distinguish this area from the very flat north
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Blooming Sunflower Fields
metas.note:
Sunflowers are grown in most of Ukraine. However, they only start to bloom as early as late July. Due to the way Ukraine was covered, this means you will usually only see sunflower fields that are in bloom in the far south and east of the country.

These fields are most common in Kherson, Mykolaiv and Odesa Oblast. The road T0403 to Nova Kakhovka especially has a lot of them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Chernobyl Coverage
metas.note:
Google sent a special car trekker to the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, where the nuclear disaster happened in the 1980s. This car goes from Ivankiv all the way to the abandoned town of Pripyat.

On most of the road to Pripyat, you will not really be able to tell that you are inside the Exclusion Zone. However, inside Pripyat you will see completely abandoned and overgrown buildings, giving the place an eerie look.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Chernobyl Road Flag
metas.note: On one side of the road going to Chernobyl, a yellow flag with an Opel logo can be seen on the Google car’s antenna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Donetsk Black Car
metas.note:
This older 2011 coverage was made with a black or white Google car, instead of the standard red one. Both cars have a long antenna.

The black car was used in Donetsk. Note that Donetsk has no newer coverage whatsoever, so never guess in that city if you see a red car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Google car leaf
metas.note: A leaf can be seen on the back of the Google car from: Ternopil to Zolochiv on the H02, Ternopil to Brody on the P39, and from Brody to Dubno on the E40. It can also be seen from Brody to Pochaiv on the P26 and from Dubno to Mlyniv on the E85.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Hungarian Architecture
metas.note: The villages close to the hungarian border have Hungarian architecture. Settlements are fairly linear and organised, with predominantly single-storey houses that are closer to the street. Many roofs have orange tiles or diamond-shaped slate tiles that are similar to roofs found in central European countries like Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Hungarian Language
metas.note: The area near the border with Hungary is majority Hungarian. As a result, you will see a lot of signs with Hungarian language on it – bilingual or even monolingual.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Ivano-Frankivsk Visual Glitch
metas.note: Within Ukraine, this visual glitch is unique to the city of Ivano-Frankivsk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Kryvyi Rih Poles
metas.note: These poles, with a red band across them, are unique to Kryvyi Rih.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Kryvyi Rih Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil can be seen on some ultra-rural dirt tracks around the iron mine in Kryvyi Rih, due to mining activity. Brazilian-style poles can also be seen, making locations around the mine very convincing bait. The foliage, however, will be significantly less tropical, and a long antenna can be seen.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Polish Bollards
metas.note:
These “Polish” bollards can be found in the Zakarpattia Oblast. They have a red reflector that wraps around the bollard.

They are identical to the standard bollard used in Poland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: The Carpathian Mountains
metas.note:
The Carpathian Mountains is an area in western Ukraine that is significantly hillier than the rest of the country, in some places bordering on mountainous.

It is also much more forested, with very little agriculture, and a lot of pine trees. The roads going through it tend to be more curvy, rather than the straight highways found in the rest of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Ukraine White Car
metas.note:
This older 2011 coverage was made with a black or white Google car, instead of the standard red one. Both cars have a long antenna.

The white car was used in Lviv, Kyiv and Kharkiv. As the coverage in these cities is mostly overwritten, the white car is quite rare.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.
